amendment.text: Bakersfield does not amend the toilet-count table (California Plumbing Code Table 422.1) or the rules on the split between men and women and on urinals. It amends one exception: where the state code lets a business or mercantile occupancy with 50 occupants or fewer have one single-user toilet room for both sexes, Bakersfield's version of exception (3) to section 422.2 sets the limit by floor area, 2,000 square feet or less.
amendment.quote: 15.09.080 Section 422.2(3) Separate facilities. Section 422.2(3) is amended to read as follows: (3) In Business and Mercantile occupancies with a total floor area of 2000 square feet or less one toilet facility designed for the use by no more than one person at a time shall satisfy the requirement for serving customers and employees of both sexes. (Ord. 4994 § 5, 2019; Ord. 4878 § 5, 2016; Ord. 4755 § 5, 2013; Ord. 4637 § 5, 2010; Ord. 4472 § 4, 2007)
amendment.state_text_replaced: (3) In business and mercantile occupancies with a total occupant load of 50 or less including customers and employees, one toilet facility, designed for use by no more than one person at a time, shall be permitted for use by both sexes. (2025 California Plumbing Code section 422.2, as quoted in research/state-codes/fixtures/los-angeles.json from https://epubs.iapmo.org/2025/CPC/#p=115)
amendment.note: The section's history stops at Ord. 4994 (2019), but section 15.09.030, re-enacted by Ord. 5204 in 2025, applies sections 15.09.040 through 15.09.080 to the 2025 edition. Exceptions (1), (2) (10 occupants or fewer, any occupancy) and (4) (all-gender room with privacy compartments) are not amended.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Unchanged from the California pack: the city amendment touches only the single-restroom exception, not Table 422.1. What changes is the alternative noted for the 50-occupant office in the state evidence: an office of 50 occupants at 150 square feet a person is 7,500 square feet, over Bakersfield's 2,000 square feet, so the single-restroom alternative does not apply to any row. The counts themselves, the 50/50 split, the urinal rule and the floor area per person come from the 2025 California Plumbing Code as read for the California pack (research/state-codes/fixtures/los-angeles.json), not from a Bakersfield document.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Bakersfield job sites. Price your restroom in five questions and see the California and city rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Bakersfield offices, schools, distribution centers and food processing plants, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Bakersfield uses California's rules, which set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Bakersfield says a building permit is required for "any construction which physically changes or adds structures to your property", and it follows California's list of work that needs none. That list covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work" and movable "partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches" high. It doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask the Building Division (661-326-3720) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Bakersfield Building Division
page.stalls_intro: Bakersfield counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for new buildings, additions and changes of use that bring in more people. In Bakersfield, an office or shop of 2,000 square feet or less may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, California's plumbing rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, and a restaurant dining room or a classroom at one per 30 square feet. Your architect or the City of Bakersfield Building Division sets the final number.
page.install_rule: Contractors working in Bakersfield pay the city business license tax and hold a California contractor license. California requires that license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Bakersfield the contractor needs a city business license and, for jobs of $1,000 or more, a California contractor license.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter in Kern County that is $54.41 an hour plus $29.91 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8.25% in Bakersfield: 7.25% statewide and 1% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Packing houses and food processing plants:** solid plastic (HDPE) or stainless steel for rooms that are washed down every day.
